{{center block/s}}</noinclude><section begin="ode2" />ment,{{page other|{{wsp|0.5em}}|{{br}}}}
And in accordance with it smote the great {{tooltip|Shang|Shāng}}.

The troops of Yin-shang{{page other|{{wsp|0.5em}}|{{br}}}}
Were collected like a forest,{{page other|{{wsp|0.5em}}|{{br}}}}
And marshalled in the wilderness of {{tooltip|Mû|Mù}}.{{page other|{{wsp|0.5em}}|{{br}}}}
We rose (to the crisis);{{page other|{{wsp|0.5em}}|{{br}}}}
'God is with you,' (said {{tooltip|Shang-fû|Shàngfù}} to the king),{{page other|{{wsp|0.5em}}|{{br}}}}
'Have no doubts in your heart<ref>See the account of the [[w:Battle of Muye|battle of Mû]] in the [[Sacred Books of the East/Volume 3/The Shu/Part 5/Book 3|third Book of the fifth Part of the Shû]]. [[w:Jiang Ziya|Shang-fû]] was one of [[w:King Wu of Zhou|Wû]]'s principal leaders and counsellors, his 'Grand-Master Shang-fû' in the next stanza.</ref>.'

The wilderness of Mû spread out extensive;{{page other|{{wsp|0.5em}}|{{br}}}}
Bright shone the chariots of sandal;{{page other|{{wsp|0.5em}}|{{br}}}}
The teams of bays, black-maned and white-bellied, galloped along;{{page other|{{wsp|0.5em}}|{{br}}}}
The Grand-Master Shang-fû{{page other|{{wsp|0.5em}}|{{br}}}}
Was like an eagle on the wing,{{page other|{{wsp|0.5em}}|{{br}}}}
Assisting king Wû,{{page other|{{wsp|0.5em}}|{{br}}}}
Who at one onset smote the great Shang.{{page other|{{wsp|0.5em}}|{{br}}}}
That morning's encounter was followed by a clear, bright (day).

{{c|{{sc|Ode 3. The {{tooltip|Mien|Mián}}.}}}}

{{smaller block/s}}
{{hanging indent/s}}
{{asc|Small beginnings and subsequent growth of the House of ''K''âu in ''K''âu. Its removal from Pin under Than-fû, with its first settlement in ''K''âu, with the place then given to the building of the ancestral temple, and the altar to the spirits of the land. Consolidation of its fortunes by king Wăn.}}

'The ancient [[w:King Tai of Zhou|duke Than-fû]]' was the grandfather of [[w:King Wen of Zhou|king Wăn]], and was canonized by the [[Author:Ji Dan|duke of ''K''âu]] as 'king Thâi.' As mentioned in a note on [[Sacred Books of the East/Volume 3/The Shih/Odes of the Temple and the Altar/The Sacrificial Odes of Kâu/Decade 1/Ode 5|p. 316]], he was the first of his family to settle in [[w:Predynastic Zhou|''K''âu]], removing there from [[w:Bin (city)|Pin]], the site of their earlier settlement, 'the country about the [[wikt:沮|''Kh''ü]] and the [[wikt:漆|''Kh''î]].'
{{smaller block/e}}
{{hanging indent/e}}

{{center block/s}}
In long trains ever increasing grow the gourds<ref>As a gourd grows and extends, with a vast development of its tendrils and leaves, so had the [[w:Ji (Zhou dynasty ancestral surname)|House of ''K''âu]] increased.</ref>.{{page other|{{wsp|0.5em}}|{{br}}}}
When (our) people first sprang,{{page other|{{wsp|0.5em}}|{{br}}}}
From the country about the {{tooltip|''Kh''ü|Jū}} and the {{tooltip|''Kh''î|Qī}}<ref name="p416_r3">These were two rivers in the territory of [[w:Bin (city)|Pin]], which name still</ref>,{{page other|{{wsp|0.5em}}|{{br}}}}
The ancient duke<section end="ode3" /><noinclude><!--¶-->
